name: Alistithmar Capital
legal_name: Alistithmar for Financial Securities and Brokerage Company (Alistithmar Capital / ICAP), a Saudi Closed Joint Stock Company
name_ar: شركة الاستثمار للأوراق المالية والوساطة (الاستثمار كابيتال)
founded: 2007 (CR 1010235995 issued in Riyadh on 22 Jul 2007; first CMA licence 7061-15 dated 2 Jun 2007, amended to licence 11156-37 on 25 Sep 2011). Converted from a limited liability company to a closed joint stock company on 10 Mar 2015.
ownership_summary: Wholly owned by The Saudi Investment Bank (SAIB). Paid-up capital SAR 250m. No debt instruments issued (SAIB Board report 2025).
government_link: Indirect. The parent SAIB is 25.61% owned by GOSI, a government social-insurance institution (see sa-saib).
group_structure: 100% subsidiary of SAIB (sa-saib) and the core of its 'Asset Management and Brokerage' segment. Manages SAIB's S60 Ventures fintech fund (USD 100m, 2025). Double counting: ICAP's assets, income and AUM are consolidated in SAIB's figures; never add this record to sa-saib. SAIB's Board report shows ICAP's net income before zakat as SAR 143.94m, against SAR 154.77m in ICAP's own statements (see discrepancies).
footprint: Saudi Arabia. Head office in Riyadh (King Fahd Branch Road, Al Aqiq per the website footer; registered address P.O. Box 6888, Riyadh 11452). Trading lounges with live price screens (website). International brokerage covers Oman, Dubai, Bahrain, Abu Dhabi, Egypt, Kuwait, USA, Qatar and Jordan. Branch count not found.
customer_segments: Retail and HNW investors (including SAIB Private Banking clients, who get fund and trading fee reductions), institutions (investment banking, discretionary mandates, brokerage), and real estate investors (real estate funds and a real estate unit-trading platform).
business_lines: FY2025 income (SAR): asset management fees net 120,038,146; brokerage fees net 67,031,330; commission income on margin and Murabaha loans 151,707,338; investment banking fees net 5,393,843; unrealised and realised gains on FVTPL investments about 4.2m; other 4,972,046; total operating income 353,309,713. Lines: brokerage (local and international) and margin finance; asset management (nine public funds, a REIT, private portfolios, private real estate funds); real estate investments; investment banking (ECM, DCM, M&A, private placements, advisory); custody; fintech venture fund management (S60 Ventures).

capabilities.wealth_summary: Alistithmar Capital is SAIB's 100%-owned CMA-licensed arm (licence 11156-37) for brokerage, asset management, margin finance, investment banking and custody. AUM was SAR 40.5bn at 31 Dec 2025 (SAR 21.7bn Shariah-approved), with a five-year CAGR of 14%. FY2025 operating income was SAR 353m and net profit SAR 134m; margin finance commission (SAR 152m, 43%), asset management fees (SAR 120m) and brokerage fees (SAR 67m) are the main lines. It runs nine public funds (equity, money market, multi-asset), a diversified REIT and private real estate funds (five launched in 2025, target asset size SAR 6bn). Traded value was SAR 85.96bn in 2025 and the firm says it ranked 4th among Saudi brokers in international-market trading. Clients trade through an 'ICAP Trade' app, a web portal, a desktop terminal and phone brokers; 2025 projects delivered a new international markets trading platform and an integrated online margin finance platform. SAIB Private Banking clients get reduced or waived fund subscription and trading fees. No robo or model-portfolio product was found.

private_banking.detail: Private banking is run by the parent bank (see sa-saib). Alistithmar Capital provides the 'special investment products' (brokerage, asset management, real estate) that SAIB lists for Private Banking clients.

asset_management.detail: AUM SAR 40,526m at 31 Dec 2025 (SAR 21,688m Shariah-approved). Public funds per the website: Saudi Companies Fund, Saudi Equity Fund, MENA Equity Fund, Flexible Saudi Equity Fund, Small and Mid-Cap Saudi Companies Fund and Parallel Market (Nomu) Companies Fund (equity); SAR Murabaha Fund (money market); Quarterly Dividend Fund and SAR Diversified Fund (multi-asset); ARIC Diversified REIT. Also private portfolios and private real estate funds. 2025 awards cited in the Directors' report include best open-ended fund in KSA for the Saudi Companies Fund (International Finance; Global Business Outlook) and best-performing equity fund for the Flexible Saudi Equity Fund (Global Business Outlook). SAIB segment: fee and other income +36% in H1 2026 on fund management fees.

brokerage.detail: Local (Tadawul main market and Nomu) and international brokerage (Oman, Dubai, Bahrain, Abu Dhabi, Egypt, Kuwait, USA, Qatar, Jordan) plus margin and Murabaha finance (SAR 1.77bn at 31 Dec 2025). Channels: web portal (online.icap.com.sa), smartphone app (iPhone, iPad, Android), 'TWS Pro 11' desktop software for active traders, phone brokers and trading lounges. FY2025 brokerage fee income SAR 67.0m (+18%); traded value SAR 85.96bn. Discounts on commissions depend on client category (fee table PDF). 2025: new international markets trading platform and integrated online margin finance platform.

digital_investing.detail: App 'ICAP Trade - الإستثمار تداول' (App Store id1320867757; Google Play com.directfn.universal_icap) with live prices, linked from the official site; web portal online.icap.com.sa; separate portals for mutual funds (MF.icap.com.sa), online account opening (oao.icap.com.sa), REIT (reit.icap.com.sa) and real estate units (re.icap.com.sa, a 'platform for trading real estate units'); desktop TWS Pro 11. The Directors' report says 2025 delivered a new international trading platform, an integrated margin finance platform (online facility requests and renewals) and improved electronic channels. The bank's own app does not list investing features (see sa-saib).

advisory.detail: CMA licence covers dealing, investment management and fund operation, arranging, advising and custody. Investment banking advisory (ECM, DCM, M&A, private placements, strategic advisory). Retail investment advice or wealth-planning services are not described on the pages read.

discretionary.detail: Private portfolios managed to an Investment Policy Guidelines document per client that sets risk and return objectives, liquidity and horizon constraints, asset allocation, exposure limits and risk controls; reviewed periodically with compliance checks. Minimums and fees not published.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or model-portfolio product found. The multi-asset Quarterly Dividend and SAR Diversified funds are the nearest diversified products.

funds_platform.detail: In-house funds only found, distributed through the fund portal, the app and SAIB. No third-party fund shelf or platform provider found.

structured_products.detail: The Shariah governance text on the team page lists 'structured products' among the Shariah-compliant offers (with funds, Murabaha and equities). No product page, issuers or terms found; SAIB's Treasury group separately manages structured products (see sa-saib).

private_markets.detail: Real estate: private funds (five launched in 2025, target asset size SAR 6bn; 'Asas' real estate fund named real estate deal of the year in KSA by International Finance), a diversified REIT and a platform for trading real estate units. S60 Ventures is a USD 100m fintech venture fund managed by Alistithmar Capital (2025). Private equity funds other than S60 not found.

islamic_wealth.detail: Shariah governance: Dar Al-Muraja'a Al-Shari'ah (Dar Al-Sharia) appointed as Shariah governance adviser; a two-member Shariah committee (Sheikh Dr. Salah Al-Shalhoub, chair, and Sheikh Dr. Sulaiman Al-Juwaisir) issues binding decisions. The fund table marks funds as Shariah-compliant; the Directors' report refers to both conventional and Shariah-compliant Saudi equity funds, so the franchise is not Shariah-only.

S60 Ventures: USD 100m fintech-focused venture fund managed by Alistithmar Capital

SAIB segment H1 2026: Asset Management and Brokerage pre-zakat income SAR 113m (+47%), fee and other income +36% on fund management fees, margin income up; segment is about 8% of SAIB operating income

Directors' report outlook: Saudi market opens to all categories of foreign investors in 2026, expected to bring liquidity; the firm continues to develop 'innovative investment solutions' and its digital infrastructure
Parent SAIB's CEO changed (Salman Al-Fughom, an ICAP board member, replaced Faisal Al-Omran, ICAP vice chairman as listed)

opportunities: 2025 delivered a new international trading platform and an integrated online margin platform; the Directors' report says it continues to develop innovative solutions and digital infrastructure (S3)
The 2026 opening of the Saudi market to all foreign investors is flagged as a growth driver (S3)
No robo, model portfolios or third-party fund shelf found; funds are in-house, with SAIB Private Banking clients offered fee discounts on funds and trading (S4, S18)
SAIB's H1 2026 outlook says it will expand fee-based businesses including asset management and brokerage; the segment's fee income grew 36% (S12)
Margin finance is 43% of operating income while brokerage fees are 19%, so fee-based wealth revenue is a stated diversification need (S2)
barriers: Trading stack appears built on DirectFN/Mubasher technology (inferred), with an in-house portal estate for funds, account opening, REIT and real estate (S19, S5)
Captive product model: in-house funds and private real estate funds; third-party products not found (S4)
Parent in transition: SAIB's CEO changed on 1 Oct 2026 and two ICAP board seats are held by the outgoing and incoming CEOs (S16, S17, S1)
Client numbers, AUM mix and 2026 interim results are not published, limiting sizing (S9)
Parent retail profitability is under pressure (H1 2026 retail pre-zakat income -69%), which may limit group technology spend (see sa-saib)
incumbent_vendors: DirectFN / Mubasher: inferred trading platform technology (S19)

discrepancies.field: ICAP net income before zakat, FY2025
discrepancies.detail: SAIB's Board report (activities of major subsidiaries) shows ICAP net income before zakat of SAR 143.94m. ICAP's own audited FS show income before zakat of SAR 154.77m (net profit SAR 134.43m).
discrepancies.resolution: Used ICAP's own statements. The SAR 10.8m difference is probably a consolidation or inter-company adjustment; not documented.

discrepancies.detail: SAIB Board report: SAR 40,526m. ICAP FS note 26: 'approximately SAR 40.52bn' (2024: SAR 38.27bn). Directors' report: about SAR 40bn. A LinkedIn snippet claims AUM above SAR 42.5bn (date unknown).
discrepancies.resolution: Used SAR 40,526m (31 Dec 2025). The SAR 42.5bn claim is undated and from a search snippet, so not recorded.

discrepancies.detail: The ICAP team page (checked 13 Oct 2026) still shows Faisal Al-Omran as vice chairman and SAIB CEO, and Salman Al-Fughom as SAIB Deputy CEO. SAIB announced on 28-29 Sep 2026 that Al-Omran left as CEO (30 Sep) and Al-Fughom became CEO (1 Oct); SAIB's Management Team page (13 Oct 2026) lists Al-Fughom as CEO and no Deputy CEO.
discrepancies.resolution: Al-Omran marked 'Conflicting sources' as ICAP vice chairman (no source says whether the seat continues); Al-Fughom's ICAP board seat kept as current with his new SAIB title noted.

discrepancies.detail: A search directory lists alistithmarcapital.com as the website; SAIB's pages and the company's own links use icap.com.sa.
discrepancies.resolution: Used icap.com.sa (opened and consistent with SAIB's links). alistithmarcapital.com refused the connection.

discrepancies.detail: The earlier record listed him as ICAP management (Head of Corporate Performance). The ICAP team page shows him on its board tab, and the Directors' report 2025 lists him as a non-executive board member whose other post is Head of Corporate Performance at SAIB.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded as ICAP non-executive board member and SAIB Head of Corporate Performance; board of six confirmed (Abunayan, Al-Omran, Al-Fughom, Chathanathan, Al-Ali, AlRayes).

discrepancies.detail: The ICAP team page describes Rakan Abunayan as chairman of MedGulf Insurance; the Directors' report 2025 lists him as Vice Chairman of MedGulf at 31 Dec 2025.
discrepancies.resolution: Both recorded in his profile; the dated Directors' report (31 Dec 2025) is the better-dated source. Minor; not material to the ICAP role.

open_items: No interim (H1 2026) company statements or AUM published; balance sheet and income are FY2025. Quarterly fund statements for 30 Sep 2026 were already posted on the site (fund-level, not company-level). Re-check after the FY2026 statements.

Number of clients, trading users, custody assets and market share are not disclosed. The firm's own claim of 4th place in international-market trading (Directors' report) is unsourced beyond that sentence.

The English version of icap.com.sa was not found (the /en path returned 404); all company pages are Arabic. Arabic text extraction from PDFs is visually ordered and a few letters were dropped (names of funds were cross-checked against the website funds table).

Vendor: DirectFN/Mubasher inference rests on the Android package ID and host names in the portal page source only. Confirm the platform vendor and scope. The App Store and Google Play listings were not opened.

English spellings of several managers are transliterated from the Arabic page and should be confirmed: LinkedIn shows 'Al-Nekhaish' (Al-Nukhaish) and 'Mutaib' (Mutab) bin Shaman; the Directors' report prints 'Shanaker' (Chathanathan); Al-Atiqi, Khani, Al-Sanae and Rajbakshi are unconfirmed.

Head of Real Estate and real estate fund managers are not named on the team page. The page (13 Oct 2026) also lists, and this pass did not profile, the Head of Compliance, AML and CFT (joined 2025), the Head of Risk (joined Feb 2025), the Head of Shared Services (re-joined May 2026) and the Shariah committee (Dr. Salah Al-Shalhoub, chair; Dr. Sulaiman Al-Juwaiser), with Dar Al-Muraja'a Al-Shari'ah named as Shariah governance provider.

LinkedIn (2026-10-13): matches recorded for the CEO (earlier pass), the Head of Investment Banking and the Head of Brokerage and Asset Management Operations (search-result titles); Al-Fughom mirrored from sa-saib. Not recorded for the Head of Asset Management, Head of Business Development (same name and employer, no title shown) or Head of Brokerage and Margin Finance (not surfaced). LinkedIn role searches for the Head of Information Technology and the chair were not run: the WebSearch quota was exhausted during this pass (X27). News checks: role-based English and Arabic searches found no 2025-2026 ICAP appointments or departures beyond the SAIB CEO change.

Product pages give no minimums, fees or model-portfolio detail; brokerage fee table PDF and fund terms and conditions were not opened. Saudi Exchange and CMA register pages were not opened (licence taken from the audited FS note 1).

Al-Omran's ICAP vice-chair seat: no source says whether he stays on the board after leaving SAIB on 30 Sep 2026, or who replaces him. ICAP's team page still shows him as SAIB CEO; re-check the page and Saudi Exchange (blocked 403 for automated reads) for an ICAP board announcement. Enterprise AM (30 Sep 2026, S17) links https://www.linkedin.com/in/faisal-al-omran-97a48415/ for him; not recorded (not an official link, profile not opened).

icap.com.sa serves an incomplete certificate chain: a plain fetch fails with 'unable to get local issuer certificate' unless the public DigiCert Global G2 TLS RSA SHA256 2020 CA1 intermediate is added to the CA bundle. Verification was not disabled.
